evidence: Oraby--Ndeffo-Mbah, BMC Infectious Diseases 26 (2026) 1430, DOI:10.1186/s12879-026-13663-2, main model and Supplementary Material 1.
correctness.rationale: The primary article's counterfactual susceptible equation contains the term \(-\nu_a\mathrm{VE}_aS_a\), while the supplementary calibration uses \(-\nu_a(S_a-S_{\infty,a})\). Solving the two scalar ODEs gives different maps from rate to endpoint. A fresh high-precision replay gives supplement rates 0.006581243690... and 0.008461585371..., but the multiplicative half-rate is 0.004968796993.... Inserting the supplement rates into the multiplicative law gives endpoints 0.1317635673... and 0.0675748848..., not 0.165 and 0.11.
risks: This is an equation-consistency result; it does not rerun the Bayesian fit or show that every reported intervention trajectory is numerically wrong.

evidence: The two printed rates overshoot the stated isolated half-target under the simulated law.
The correct multiplicative half-rate is age-independent under the source's common efficacy and common target ratio.
value.rationale: The disputed calibration is used to interpret reactive-vaccination intensities in a current outbreak model. Distinguishing a positive-asymptote relaxation law from the actually simulated multiplicative vaccine-removal law changes the claimed mapping between daily rate and susceptible reduction, so the correction has substantive modelling value.
risks: The source's separately explored policy-rate scenarios remain mathematically admissible; this audit does not evaluate their epidemiological effectiveness.

final_claim: In the Oraby--Ndeffo-Mbah Texas measles study, the supplementary reactive-vaccination rate calibration is derived from an affine relaxation law with positive asymptote, whereas the main counterfactual model and released implementation use multiplicative susceptible removal by vaccine efficacy. Therefore the supplement's age-specific half-susceptibility rates do not calibrate the simulated vaccination equation; at 150 days and efficacy 0.93 the multiplicative half-reduction rate is 0.004968796993... per day for both age groups.
limitations: No Bayesian refit or full epidemic resimulation.
Infection is switched off only to compare the source's own isolated calibration laws.
